products.name: Dell Thunderbolt Dock WD22TB4
products.summary: Dell's WD22TB4 is a modular Thunderbolt 4 dock for managed business fleets: its host connection module can be swapped to upgrade the dock instead of replacing it. It offers the widest native display mix here, with two DisplayPort outputs, HDMI and a multifunction USB-C display port, and charges Dell laptops at up to 130W. There is no card reader, reflecting its IT-deployment focus.

evidence.note: Dell official user guide specifications: USB Type-C ports are 1x USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-C, 2x Type-C with Thunderbolt 4 and 1x USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-C with DisplayPort 1.4 Alt Mode (= 4 downstream USB-C ports; the host connection is the dock's attached cable module and is not in this list); USB Type-A ports 2x USB 3.2 Gen1 plus 1x Gen1 with PowerShare (=3); video ports include 2x DisplayPort 1.4 and 1x HDMI 2.0; external displays supported up to 4; network is Gigabit Ethernet. Power delivery is stated as 130W to Dell systems and 90W to non-Dell systems with the 180W adapter - the recorded 130W is Dell's headline published rating, with the 90W non-Dell figure noted here. The complete specification list contains no SD or microSD reader, hence false for both. No safety listing stated in the maker specifications.
Manufacturer Specs section states Output 120W Max, 2 USB-C Ports, 1 USB-A Port, one-port charging USB-C 1/USB-C 2: 100W Max, and lists Anker GaNPrime GaN Technology.

Anker service page confirms Total Output 120W Max and single-port USB-C output 20V/5A (100W Max). No UL, ETL, CSA, TUV, SGS, CE, UKCA or FCC safety certification for the charger is stated on the manufacturer product or service pages opened, so certification is recorded as none/not_certified.

products.name: Anker 737 Charger (GaNPrime 120W)
products.summary: A three-port GaNPrime wall charger built around two USB-C ports and one USB-A port, aimed at charging a laptop alongside a phone and tablet from a single outlet. Either USB-C port can deliver up to 100W on its own, while the unit shares a 120W ceiling across all connected devices.

evidence.note: Manufacturer Specs state Single Port Output USB-C 1 (65W Max) / USB-C 2 (65W Max) / USB-A (22.5W Max), with dual- and triple-port splits that stay within the charger's 65W rating given in the product name; the page describes GaN II technology in the product copy (full text seen on the CA variant of the same page).
No safety-certification body from the controlled vocabulary is stated on the manufacturer product page opened, so certification is recorded as none/not_certified.

products.name: Anker 735 Charger (Nano II 65W)
products.summary: A compact three-port charger using GaN II technology, with two USB-C ports and one USB-A port in a pocketable body. A single USB-C connection can supply up to 65W for a USB-C laptop, and the charger redistributes its 65W total when two or three devices are attached.

evidence.note: Manufacturer spec table (SKU 40747, the CD226 charger) states USB-C1/C2 output up to 100W Max with PD 3.0/PPS, USB-C3 and USB-A at 22.5W max, Wattage 100 watts, 4 total USB ports; the comparison table on the same page confirms 3 x USB-C + 1 x USB-A and GaN positioning in the product title.

The page lists fire-protection class UL94-V0, which is a material flammability rating and not a UL/ETL safety certification of the charger; no certification body from the controlled vocabulary is claimed for the charger itself, so certification is recorded as none/not_certified.

products.name: UGREEN Nexode 100W GaN Charger
products.summary: A four-port GaN wall charger with three USB-C ports and one USB-A port, sized for a laptop plus phones and accessories. Its first two USB-C ports can each reach 100W when used alone, with the full 100W shared across ports as more devices are connected.

evidence.note: Manufacturer product page states 2x USB-C and 2x USB-A ports, 108W of total power output, integrated GaN technology and USB-C PD 3.0.

Belkin's official FAQ for WCH010 states total power output 108W and single USB-C port output up to 20.5V/4.7A (96.35W), published by Belkin as up to 96W per port. The FAQ's only certification mention is MFi, which is not in the controlled body vocabulary, and no UL/ETL/CSA/TUV/SGS/CE/UKCA/FCC safety certification is stated, so certification is recorded as none/not_certified.

products.name: Belkin BoostCharge Pro 4-Port GaN Charger 108W
products.summary: A desktop-style GaN charger with two USB-C and two USB-A ports on a 2-metre power cord, designed to sit on a desk rather than hang from an outlet. It delivers up to 96W from a single USB-C port for a laptop and shares 108W in total across up to four devices using Intelligent Power Sharing.

evidence.note: Anker service page for A2341 lists a single output specification set, 5V/9V/15V/20V/28V up to 5A (140W Max), with PD and PPS charging technology, consistent with the single USB-C port design; the linked A2341 user manual describes achieving max power from a single port.

Manufacturer product page presents the 717 as a GaNPrime-series charger with a 140W max output and Power Delivery 3.1 compatibility. No safety-certification body from the controlled vocabulary is stated on the manufacturer pages opened, so certification is recorded as none/not_certified.

products.name: Anker 717 Charger (140W)
products.summary: A single-port GaNPrime charger built for high-power USB-C laptops, delivering up to 140W through USB Power Delivery 3.1, including the 28V profile used by the 16-inch MacBook Pro. It trades multi-port flexibility for maximum single-device speed in a body notably smaller than Apple's own 140W adapter.

evidence.note: Apple's product page overview states this 1.8-meter cable features a black braided design, supports Thunderbolt 3, Thunderbolt 4 and USB 4 data transfer up to 40Gb/s, and charging up to 100W; it is a USB-C to USB-C cable.

products.name: Apple Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) Pro Cable (1.8 m)

evidence.note: Manufacturer page's Technical Specifications table lists the 0.8m variant with Max. Performance 40Gb/s and Power Delivery Ability 100 Watts (20 Volts @ 5 Amps), for use with USB-C devices over a USB-C connector.

products.name: CalDigit Thunderbolt 4 Cable (0.8m)
products.summary: CalDigit's short 0.8-metre Thunderbolt 4 cable is aimed at dock and desktop setups where excess cable is clutter. It carries up to 40Gb/s across Thunderbolt 4, Thunderbolt 3 and USB4, and supplies up to 100W of power delivery, with E-Marker chips at both ends managing safe power negotiation.

evidence.note: Belkin's official CAB015 page states support for up to 240W Power Delivery fast charging, high-speed data transfers up to 480 Mbps on the USB 2.0 standard, a nylon braided design, and variants CAB015bt1MWH/CAB015bt1MBK at 3.3 ft / 1 m. products.name: Belkin BoostCharge USB-C to USB-C Cable 240W (1m)

evidence.note: Belkin's official CAB025 page states 240W Power Delivery, a 95% PCR PET braided exterior, and available lengths including 3.28 ft / 1M.

Belkin's official CAB025 FAQ confirms a USB-C to USB-C connector, maximum power up to 240W (48V/5A), and USB 2.0 data transfer speeds up to 480 Mbps. It also states the cable is USB-IF certified; USB-IF is outside the safety-certification body vocabulary, so no certification trio is recorded.

products.name: Belkin BoostCharge Eco USB-C to USB-C Braided Cable 240W (1m)

products.name: UGREEN USB-C to USB-C Cable 100W Braided (2m)
